program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 1000

source_provenance: PubMed systematic reviews/meta-analyses and historical counterevidence

policy.validation_strategy: cheap PMID/entity screening during authoring; full repository validation only after Wave 1000

waves.focus: 2024 systematic review of chromium in T2D; possible glycemic/lipid signals coexist with wide formulation/dose/duration heterogeneity and uncertain long-term risk.
2025 overweight/obesity meta-analysis; selected insulin-resistance/metabolic effects with several near-null estimates and mixed anthropometric/BP/liver findings.
2025 dose-response meta-analysis of 10 RCTs; BP reduction was much larger in hypertensive than normotensive participants, emphasizing baseline-BP dependence.
Systematic review/meta-analysis of vitamin-K supplementation and cardiovascular risk factors; biomarker/risk-factor evidence is not clinical-event prevention evidence.
Updated randomized-trial meta-analysis of inflammatory mediators; inflammatory biomarker evidence remains surrogate and population dependent.
2026 randomized-trial meta-analysis in metabolic diseases; cardiometabolic, inflammatory and oxidative-stress findings remain phenotype- and endpoint-specific.
2025 dose-response meta-analysis of 27 experimental human studies on blood lipids; possible nonlinear lipid effects and overexposure concerns remain first-class.
75-study GRADE meta-analysis; several glycemic/lipid/inflammatory/oxidative markers improved while LDL, HDL, insulin, BP and liver enzymes were null.
2026 13-study/14,539-participant CHD meta-analysis of folic acid+B6+B12; homocysteine lowering and vascular outcomes remain distinct from hard-event efficacy.
21-RCT/1,625-participant meta-analysis; isolated B12 lowered homocysteine, a surrogate biomarker, without implying cardiovascular-event reduction.
2026 36-RCT hyperhomocysteinemia meta-analysis; tHcy and modest BP/lipid surrogate changes with high heterogeneity/bias and no adjudicated hard cardiovascular endpoints.
Randomized-trial meta-analysis found little overall lipid benefit, increased SBP, and selected LDL/TC subgroup effects—important cardiovascular-safety counterweight.
Ten-RCT/526-participant cardiometabolic-disease meta-analysis; insulin/HOMA-IR/HDL signals with FPG, TC, TG, LDL and VLDL nulls and high heterogeneity.
20-RCT GRADE dose-response review; fasting-insulin/QUICKI signals with FBS, HbA1c and HOMA-IR nulls.
Ten-RCT/509-participant T2D meta-analysis of glucose/lipid outcomes; disease-specific evidence with formulation and trial-quality limitations.
28-study T2D meta-analysis; FPG/insulin/HbA1c/HOMA-IR pooled reductions accompanied by extreme heterogeneity for several outcomes.
Older diabetes meta-analysis including mono- and combination supplementation; glycemic/lipid signals with inadequate long-term safety evidence and combination uncertainty.
22-study/41,633-participant BP meta-analysis; small SBP/DBP reductions with dose/duration/subgroup variability—large sample but surrogate outcome.
Hypertension-specific meta-analysis; BP lowering was stronger with lower baseline potassium, higher sodium and no antihypertensive therapy.
23-RCT/1,213-participant essential-hypertension meta-analysis; modest BP reduction with moderate heterogeneity and adjunctive-context framing.
Umbrella/hierarchical synthesis of nutrient supplements for T2D; most HbA1c evidence was low or very-low certainty and intervention-specific.
Observational dose-response meta-analysis found a U-shaped association between blood selenium and metabolic syndrome; association evidence must not be treated as supplementation efficacy.
Observational GRADE dose-response meta-analysis linked higher dietary calcium with lower MetS odds; dietary association is not supplement-trial evidence.
Earlier cardiometabolic RCT meta-analysis; glycemic/lipid signals with BP/anthropometric nulls, useful historical comparison with newer zinc syntheses.
Older metabolic-disease RCT meta-analysis of glucose/lipid profiles; retained as historical evidence to compare with later contradictory selenium syntheses.
